            normalized to E.164 form: separators are stripped, a leading '+'

                characters of the SHA-256 digest over the owner's normalized last

                owner was created, i.e. before this create. Zero when the name
                was unique on creation.

              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

                ranging from 1 to 3. It starts at 1, gains 1 when an email
                address is present, gains 1 when the owner had no namesakes at

              readOnly: true

                duplicate at creation: it was not a hard duplicate, yet it
                shared an existing owner's lastName and postcode while carrying a
                different telephone. Otherwise false.

                not a possible duplicate.
              type: integer

              example: 1
              readOnly: true

              type: string

              readOnly: true

              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||A1B2C3D4E5F6A7B8'
              readOnly: true

              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:

              readOnly: true
          required:

        firstName:
          title: First name

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^\s*\S[\s\S]*$'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '^\s*\S[\s\S]*$'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: separators are stripped, a leading '+'
            keeps the supplied country code otherwise '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped, and the result must carry 8 to 15
            digits after the '+'. For example '0412 345 678' is stored and
            returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '0412345678'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation"
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; when present it must be four
            digits and, for a city whose region is known (Sydney->NSW,
            Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), fall within that region's inclusive
            postcode range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city
            with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and
            returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted the server's current date is used.
            When supplied it must not be later than the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-30'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.PastOrPresent"
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date

          format: date

            shares its household (same last name and postcode). It only bypasses
            the household-duplicate block; the owner is then created as a declared
            household member and is not flagged as a possible duplicate. Optional
            and write-only; defaults to false.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true

              title: Customer code

              title: Membership number

            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-

              description: >-

                owner was created, i.e. before this create. Zero when the name
                was unique on creation.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level assigned at creation,
                ranging from 1 to 3. It starts at 1, gains 1 when an email
                address is present, gains 1 when the owner had no namesakes at

              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3

              readOnly: true

              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when this owner was flagged a possible (soft-match)

              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

              enum:

              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||A1B2C3D4E5F6A7B8'
              readOnly: true

## Summary

I implemented `telephoneDisplay` as a read-only, human-formatted rendering of the owner's stored E.164 telephone, leaving raw `telephone` untouched.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `telephoneDisplay` string property to the `Owner` schema (the DTOs are generated from this spec), documenting the format and that `telephone` stays E.164.

2. **`TelephoneNormalizer.java`** — Added `toDisplay(String e164)`, which strips to digits, splits off the country code (recognising `+61` → 2 digits and `+1` → 1 digit, defaulting to 2), and joins the country code with the national digits grouped in threes: `+61412345678` → `+61 412 345 678`. Returns `null` for null/empty input.

3. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — Wired a `formatTelephoneDisplay` MapStruct qualifier (matching the existing derived-field pattern like `formatDisplayName`) that delegates to `TelephoneNormalizer.toDisplay(owner.getTelephone())`.

The acceptance test `coreFormatsTelephoneDisplay` now passes: `$.telephone` = `+61412345678`, `$.telephoneDisplay` = `+61 412 345 678`. Full suite: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.
